cells.place: Da, Findspot: Kakkalūr, Yalbarga Taluk, Raichur District.
cells.remarks: Records the gift made by Kundanāmi, the elder sister of Ereyappa, to the village Adagūru, situated in Dhavala-viṣaya to the brāhmaṇa Ādityabhaṭṭa, a devotee of the temple of Kāḍyapa-gōtra. Seems to state that a sum of 90 diadems comprising the dhruva-kaṭaka according to the kaṭṭaja of Kukkama-nūru, for purposes of the village, was to be paid every year provided to the king. The village seems to have been stated to have obtained the village from the king. The donor is described as ruling over Gaṅgakandarppadeva-viṣaya and Gaṅgāpāḍi-96,000. The record was written by Eye-yappa, son of Āyapadēva, and a disciple of Udayanandi. The engraver of the record was Kannada.

cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Agali on the right bank of the river, to the brāhmaṇa Dēvaśarman of Nandisēnavarman, who was the resident of Kēśammāḍi and who belonged to Kāḍyapa-gōtra. It is stated that the king gave the gift with the approval of his brother Nāgavarman's sons, viz., Mūlādēva and Mārasarman to whom he gave the gift village which was approved by the king. The writer was Viśvakarmācārya who was also a sculptor. A paddy field having the sowing capacity of two khaṇḍukas. Published in Ep. Ind., vol. XXXVII, pp. 133 ff., and plate.

cells.remarks: Late. Issued from Puṇḍravardhana in the Śiṅgāvaravīthī by Ayudaka who was a resident of Puṇḍravardhana and was the holder of Guṇḍamagandhikā and Śaṅkaraghoṣikā. Records a grant of one kuḷavāpa of land by purchase, by three persons of Puṇḍravardhana, namely Keśamaka, a resident of Guṇḍamagandhikā, Bhōyila and Mahīdāsa, residents of Guṇḍamagandhikā for repairs to the temple of Śaṅkarasvāmī at the temple of Sahasrarāśmi (the Sun-god) at Guṇḍamagandhikā. The document was written by Budhadāsa and the plate was prepared by the engraver, a goldsmith. Published in the Bāṅglā Academy Patrikā, Dacca University, Māgha-Chaitra, B.S. 1370, pp. 36 ff., and plates; Ep. Ind., Vol. XXVIII, pp. 247 ff., and plates.

cells.remarks: Incomplete. Only one plate is available. Records the grant of a village named Laghu-Vāḍa, which was the half of the village Thikkarikā of two persons (names perhaps mentioned in the lost plate) for their own merit and for the merit of his parents. Probably the grant of the said two villages was made on the occasion of the death anniversary of Mōmaladēvī. The ḍēṭāka, Pārchika Ṭhakura Vāmanasvāmin, Ṭhakura Puruṣōttama, Ṭhakura Dēvadatta are mentioned in the record. Published in the Bhandarkar's List, No. 234.

cells.date: 1) Vikrama 1191, Kārttika śu. 8. 2) Vikrama 1200, Śrāvaṇa śu. 15, Monday=1144 A.D., July 16.
cells.remarks: Do. Only the first plate is available. Records that the village Vaḍanā and Uthavaṇaka belonging respectively to Suriṣaṇī and Suvarṇaprāsādikā and both situated in Rājāyana bhōga in Mahādēvāda maṇḍala were granted to Ācārya Dhanaśāla, the son of Viśvarūpa and grandson of Ṭhakkura Mahādēva, a Brāhmaṇa of the Bhāradvāja-gōtra with three pravaras, Āśvalāyana-śākhā, was a student of two Vēdas, was a Karṇāṭaka-brāhmaṇa from the south and who had migrated from Adrēśaviddhi. The grant was made by the Mahākumāra on the occasion of the funeral ceremonies of his father Mahādēva Naravarmmadēva on the first date. The said grant was confirmed on the second date by Mahākumāra Lakshmīvarmmadēva. Published in ibid., pp. 301 ff.; Bhandarkar's List, Nos. 239 and 257.

cells.place: No. 2. Ślōga śigh. Findspot: Mōṭā Darwāzā
cells.date: Vikrama 1273, Vaiśākha śu. 4, Friday=1216 A.D., April 22. (The year was Chaitrādi).
cells.remarks: Fragmentary and damaged. Records the construction of two temples one to the god Vishnu and the other to the god Śiva by the king Bhīmadēva for the merit of his mother Rōhiṇī and father Vālapā who gave great favour to of the king Kumārapāla. Also gives the genealogical accounts of both the king and his minister. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. II, pp. 439 ff.

cells.place: The stepwell called Gaurikuṇḍa in the same place. Black stone slab containing figures of 3 couples, built into the western wall.
cells.remarks: Right side broken and in two parts. Upper portion contains the names of the couples viz. (1) Dēvaśā and his wife Chamuṇḍādēvī, daughter of Rudrapāṭa. (2) Sōmaśā, son of Jagaśā and his wife Sītādēvī, daughter of Sāhaṇī, and (3) Nāgapaṭa, son of Nāyā. Also the renovation of the two shrines of the goddess Dēvī along with Puskara tīrtha (i.e., probably the step-well) by Mahāṁ- Jayata, son of Sādhu [Sō]madha by means of his money. It also mentions the performance of religious rites. The names of some persons like Brihat-Purusha Rāja śrī Khāṇḍadēva, Ganda śrī Brihaspati, etc. In characters of about the 13th century. Cf. Inscriptions of Kathiawad, No. 19.

cells.place:
Slab built into the outer wall of the Yādava
Pāpāḍēśvarī temple.
cells.remarks: Records that the astrologer of the Yādava king, Changadēva by name, who was a descendant of Bhāskarācārya founded a college (maṭha) for the study of the Siddhānta-śāstra and other works of his grandfather and relatives (not named), and that the college was endowed in Śaka 1128 (wrong for 1129), Śravana, śu. 15, lunar eclipse, corresponding to 1207 A.D., August 9, with land and village in the village, by Sōidēva, the son of Gōvana (III), belonging to the Nikumbha Bhā family. Sōidēva's younger brother Hēmādridēva is reported to be governing a district containing sixteen hund- red villages after the death of the former. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. I, pp. 388-48.

cells.place: South wall, tripaṭṭa and jagatī
cells.date: Śaka 1180 (for 1188), Kehaya, Chittirai 17 (for 24), Hasta, Thursday=1266 A.D., April 18.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village, Jālapalli, the tank at Viṇṇamangalam and some lands in the big tank at Tombalur to god Tripurāntaka-perumāḷ of Tombalur alias Dēśimāṇikka-paṭṭaṇam and his wife Pārpat-cheṭṭichchiyār to save Nambi Iravichchiyār, Śīdēvi-yakkan and their dependants from rebirth (punarāvritti) and for the merit of the arms and sword of Tribhuvanamalla-vīra-Rāmanātha. The priest Irāmaṇiyār was to manage the settlement of lands gifted to the priest Irāmaṇiyār Āḷḷāḷanambiyār and other servants of the temple. A postscript states that the priest leased one-third of his share to Śavarippurumal-nambiyār. Same as A. R. Ep., 1891, No. 9 and published in Ep. Carn., Vol. IX, Bn. 10.

cells.remarks: Records the royal order to the nāḍugaḷ and thānattār of the temples in the various nāḍus, exempting the dāna-mānya lands from the taxes such as siddhāyam, kāṇikkai etc. to provide for various services such as worship, food offerings, etc. of the respective gods. Further records the gift of village-lands (kāṇiyāṭci) by Chokkappa-perumāḷ including those of the Sōmanāthadēvar in the village and also income from taxes to god Chokkappa-perumāḷ of the village for the prosperity of the king and his country. Noticed in Arch. Sur. Mys., A. R., 1911, p. 50.

cells.place: Dīdi... Vaikuṇṭhaperumāḷ temple, north and south walls, tripatta stones.
cells.remarks: Do. Records three gifts made to the deities. Śrī-Kṛishṇar and others: 1) by the sabhā of the village, the Tiruvēṅkaṭamuḍaiyān of Tyāgankuḍi 1) of a perpetual lamp by Uruppiṇi, the wife of Sēṇan Namban of Tyāgankuḍi 2) of 90 sheep for a lamp by an individual (name not clear) entrusted to a native of Āḷappirandān-kūḍal and 3) of land by another individual for food offerings in the midday, purchased and made tax-free by payments of gold to the sabhāyār. In characters of about the 10th century.

cells.place:
UTTAR PRADESH
JHAMOLI DISTRICT
JOSHIMATH TAHSIL
Mana.—A stone slab in the village
cells.remarks: Fragmentary and damaged. Refers to a king. Relates to the conduct of trade between the "Rongpa" (the people of the valley) and the "traders". Seems to record the levy imposed probably on the people of the valley if the loads of separate traders fell short that was recognized and must be caught. In case the thief was caught his hand should be cut off.

cells.king: Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Vijaya-dēva ruling from Valadurga, Kōlhāpur.
cells.date: (1) Śaka 1112, Sādhāraṇa, Pauṣya ba. 12, Tuesday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti. Amṛtēśvaramūri—Umāmāhēśvari for feeding the students and for keeping the mathe in good repair. (2) Śaka 1114, Paridhāvin, Āśvija śu. 1, Friday. Irregular. (3) Śaka 1118, Piṅgala, Śaka year was 1116. February 3.
cells.remarks: Contains three parts. First part records that the king granted in the village of Kopparavāḍa in Ēḍenāḍu to four brāhmaṇas (named) who had settled at a matha founded by Nāyaka Lōkaṇa for worshipping Amṛtēśvaramūri—Umāmāhēśvara, for feeding the students and for keeping the mathe in good repair. The second part records a gift of some land on the second date in the Village-kholla by the above Nāyaka Lōkaṇa in favour of the same four brāhmaṇas. The last section records a gift of some land on the third date, to the same brāhmaṇas by the same Nāyaka Lōkaṇa for feeding the students studying the Vēdas. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. III, p. 213 ff.

cells.remarks: Refers to the rule of the Rājānaka Lakṣmaṇachandra of Trigarta and records the construction of the temple and donations to the temple by the merchant Mayuka and his younger brother Ahuka, the sons of Siddha and Chinna. The masons Miyaka and Thōdhuka built the temple. Composed by the poet Rājānaka Rāma, son of Bhūrigaka. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. I, pp. 11 ff., Bhandarkar's List, No. 1438.

cells.remarks: Damaged. Probably records the grant of income from Phulhalli village belonging to Kumvara Pālhaṇadēva and others to the temple at Bhallārakē Dēvēśvara (of the temple) of Kṣēmadēvarā. Also records the grant of a tax called gaṇḍāyam by Tālāra Pāthada. Mentions two witnesses named Vaijara, the son of Vāhaḍa and Dēdā, the son of Dēdā. cells.date: 1272, Jyēṣṭha ba. 11, Friday, May 24, 1215 A.D., May 24, f.d.t. 86.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a stepwell (vāpī) in the Dammā-bhūmi, to the east of Haridēvagrāma, by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara, who was the son of the Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kaḷuvārajadēva, who belonged to the Dadhīcha family and to the town Mām-gaḷāka. Also states that two taxes wa. one oil on each ghāṇaka (oil mill) working within the boundaries of the village and oil mill working within the boundaries of the village (dharmmārtham). States that śrī-dāra Āmala caused the bandhana (probably of the edge of the slab) and the name of the scribe (son of the writer of the record) and the Subaḍa of the Naigama anvaya wrote the record. Published in ibid., Vol. XLI, pp. 85 ff; Bhandarkar's List, No. 465.

cells.location: Mount Abū
cells.place: Vimala Vasahī. White stone slab built into a niche in the corridor.
cells.date: Vikrama 1287 (Current), Laukika, Phālguna ba. 3, Sunday=1230 A.D., March 3.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of the Nēminātha temple on the Arbuda-chala by Tējapāla of the Prāgvāṭa family on the Anahilapāṭa for the merit of his wife Anupamā and their son Lāvaṇyasiṁha. Gives account of the family of Tējapāla. The genealogy of the Chaulukya kings of the vāśī is also given. The text was composed by Chandravasudēva, whose feet were honoured by the Chaulukya king. It was engraved by Chandēśvara, son of Dhānēśvara and grandson of Kēśava, of the Nāgēndra-gachchha, and written by Vijayasiṁha-sūri of the Nāgēndra-gachchha. Published in ibid., p. 208 ff. and plate; Bhandarkar's List, No. 487.

cells.place: Mosque in Mahalla Daraganj. Slab in the facade.
cells.remarks: States that this Jami'-mosque was first repaired under the orders of emperor Shah Jahan by Sayyid Zabiru'd-Din Muhammad Rida Bukhari. It was lying desolate for some time on account of the (vandalism of the) adversaries (non-Muslims?), until the time of the king when a royal order, accompanied by a grant, was issued for its repair. On the representation made in person in the royal court by Sayyid Nagru'd-Din 'Ali, a grandson of the aforesaid Sayyid. The work was started on the given date under the order and supervision of the grandson of Muhammad Mu'min at a cost of two thousand and seven hundred rupees. Written by Khurshid 'Ali.

cells.place: Headstone of the grave of Sayyid Miran Muhyu'd-Din in the compound of the Shāhi-Masjid.
cells.remarks: States that this Foot-Print on stone of the Holy Prophet was set up by Miyan Humayun Khan-i-Khanan Qadiri Farmuli. The latter was asked some time in the quoted year by the Prophet in dream that the Print should be brought from the distant place and set up in the mosque. He accordingly dedicated to his (i.e. Prophet's) son i.e. the saint. Name of the scribe illegible.
